metadata.summary: Two senior executives at different top-level Premier League clubs have told Sky Sports News they would be "staggered" and "amazed" if 15 clubs were prepared to vote to expel Manchester City from the league, with such a move akin to a "self-inflicted commercial disaster".
metadata.content: Man City charges: Premier League executives would be 'staggered' if clubs vote for expulsion as punishment | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Exclusive Man City charges: Premier League executives would be 'staggered' if clubs vote for expulsion as punishment Sky Sports News understands that discussions remain ongoing within, and between, the bosses of other clubs in the Premier League about how they might react to developments in the Man City case; City's commercial appeal is seen as playing a key role in the attraction of the Premier League Rob Dorsett Football Correspondent @RobDorsettSky Thursday 1 October 2026 09:39, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rob Dorsett reports two senior executives at different top-level Premier League clubs would be 'amazed' 15 clubs would vote to expel Manchester City. Two senior executives at different top-level Premier League clubs have told Sky Sports News they would be "staggered" and "amazed" if 15 clubs were prepared to vote to expel Manchester City from the league, with such a move akin to a "self-inflicted commercial disaster". Expulsion is one of several punishments available to the independent commission, which earlier this week found Man City guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought against them over alleged financial mismanagement. messages.text: Former Wallaby hooker Charles confirms MND diagnosis

metadata.summary: Former Australia rugby international Nathan Charles, who overcame cystic fibrosis to forge a professional career in a contact sport, has been diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND).
metadata.content: Nathan Charles: Former Australia rugby international reveals motor neurone disease diagnosis | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Nathan Charles: Former Australia rugby international reveals motor neurone disease diagnosis Nathan Charles has revealed his motor neurone disease (MND) diagnosis; the 37-year-old made four appearances for Australia across 2014 and 2015; Charles overcame cystic fibrosis to produce a decorated career in professional rugby Thursday 1 October 2026 08:23, UK Image: Nathan Charles made four appearances for Australia across 2014 and 2015 Former Australia rugby international Nathan Charles, who overcame cystic fibrosis to forge a professional career in a contact sport, has been diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND). The 37-year-old Charles, who made his Test debut in 2014 and earned four caps for the Wallabies, including a 12-12 draw against New Zealand, revealed he has been diagnosed with the same illness as recently retired National Rugby League star Jai Arrow. MND is an umbrella term for a group of progressive neurological conditions where the motor neurones degenerate. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is the most common form, and ALS is often called Lou Gehrig's disease. During an interview with former Wallabies lock and now commentator Justin Harrison on Stan Sport this week, Charles revealed he had only recently been diagnosed. metadata.summary: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua finally came face-to-face on Wednesday - but few could have predicted how their first press conference ahead of their blockbuster heavyweight clash would unfold.
metadata.content: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Rivals show respect at friendly first press conference - but how long will it last? | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Rivals show respect at friendly first press conference - but how long will it last? Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will finally settle their rivalry in a British heavyweight blockbuster at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff on Friday December 11; Fury and Joshua both traded taunts at their first press conference in London; the British duo then shared a face-off Thursday 1 October 2026 07:28, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the best bits from the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua press conference. Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua finally came face-to-face on Wednesday - but few could have predicted how their first press conference ahead of their blockbuster heavyweight clash would unfold. Perhaps because of the uncertainty that has continued to surround the fight since it was announced, there was something of a surreal atmosphere in west London until the two biggest names in British boxing finally appeared on stage shortly after 6pm. The whole thing suddenly felt very real, with the audible excitement of the relatively small number of fans who had been able to buy tickets to watch from the arena's upper tier clearly appreciated by both fighters. messages.text: Somerset pair Overton and Luff win PCA awards

metadata.summary: Somerset duo Craig Overton and Sophie Luff have won the headline accolades at the 2026 PCA awards in partnership with Toyota while emerging England stars Sonny Baker and Tilly Corteen-Coleman also received coveted honours at Exhibition White City.
metadata.content: 2026 PCA awards: Somerset duo Craig Overton and Sophie Luff win headline accolades at Exhibition White City | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content 2026 PCA awards: Somerset duo Craig Overton and Sophie Luff win headline accolades at Exhibition White City Craig Overton and Sophie Luff win the headline accolades at the 2026 PCA awards to complete a Somerset double; England's Sonny Baker and left-arm spinner Tilly Corteen-Coleman claim Young Player of the Year awards Wednesday 30 September 2026 16:57, UK Image: Craig Overton and Sophie Luff won the headline accolades at Exhibition White City on Wednesday Somerset duo Craig Overton and Sophie Luff have won the headline accolades at the 2026 PCA awards in partnership with Toyota while emerging England stars Sonny Baker and Tilly Corteen-Coleman also received coveted honours at Exhibition White City. Overton saw him collect a PCA awards quadruple, winning the PCA Men's Player of the Year trophy, the PCA Men's Domestic Overall MVP, the Rothesay County Championship Player of the Year and selection in the IG PCA Men's Team of the Year. The 32-year-old, who has scored 951 runs, taken 76 wickets and 45 catches across all three formats this season, becomes the first Somerset player to secure the award since Nick Compton in 2012, beating competition from the notable shortlist of players including Joe Clarke, George Hill and Dan Lawrence.
